rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Algae are thalloid, chlorophyll-bearing aquatic producers classified by accessory pigments into green (Chlorophyceae — chl a+b, starch, freshwater, Spirogyra), brown (Phaeophyceae — fucoxanthin, mannitol/laminarin, marine, Sargassum) and red (Rhodophyceae — r-phycoerythrin, floridean starch, deep marine, Gelidium) algae.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Spirogyra has a spiral chloroplast with pyrenoids. Sexual reproduction is conjugation: a tube joins two filaments and a zygospore results. That is not a seed.
Gelidium and related red algae supply agar. Brown algae supply algin and iodine-rich kelp. Green algae share chlorophyll a and b and store starch, which is why they sit nearest the land plants.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Algae vs plants:** algae have no roots, stems, leaves, vascular tissue or embryos — a thallus; "plants" in the strict sense begin with bryophytes.  ·  **Pyrenoid vs nucleus:** pyrenoids are protein bodies inside chloroplasts around which starch forms; the nucleus is suspended in the cell centre of Spirogyra.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Match the organism to the character.  ·  A product does not move an organism into another kingdom.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** What are pyrenoids? **Answer.** **Proteinaceous bodies embedded in the chloroplast** around which starch is synthesised and stored — the algal equivalent of a starch-forming centre. Characteristic of *Spirogyra*, whose ribbon chloroplasts carry a row of pyrenoids.  ·  **Short answer (2m):** Why are red algae able to live at greater depths? **Answer.** Their pigment **r-phycoerythrin** absorbs the **blue-green light** that penetrates deepest into clear ocean water — exactly the wavelengths green chlorophyll cannot use efficiently.…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Pigments decide depth:** phycoerythrin harvests deep-penetrating blue-green light, letting red algae live deeper than green or brown.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Algae: thalloid, autotrophic, chlorophyll a universal; classified by accessory pigments.  ·  Green (Chlorophyceae): chl a+b, starch, motile with equal flagella, freshwater — Spirogyra, Chlamydomonas.  ·  Brown (Phaeophyceae): chl a+c + fucoxanthin, mannitol/laminarin, marine — Sargassum, Laminaria.  ·  Red (Rhodophyceae): chl a+d + r-phycoerythrin, floridean starch, non-motile, deep marine — Polysiphonia, Gelidium.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Marine algae/phytoplankton produce roughly half of the world's oxygen.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Economic: agar (Gelidium), carrageenin (Chondrus), algin (Laminaria), iodine (kelp), food (Porphyra, Chlorella), fertiliser, oxygen/food-chain base.  ·  Spirogyra: unbranched filament; spiral ribbon chloroplasts with pyrenoids; central vacuole with suspended nucleus; conjugation → zygospore → meiosis (haplontic).  ·  **Zygospore vs zygote:** the zygote is the immediate fused cell; the zygospore is its thick-walled resting stage.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Scalariform vs lateral conjugation:** scalariform = between cells of two parallel filaments (ladder-like); lateral = between adjacent cells of one filament.  ·  ***Gelidium*** — the agar weed.  ·  The pigment-classification question (2024) needs exactly: class name + pigment + one example × 3 — nothing more is required for 3 marks.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: "Accessory pigments are depth adapters — each colour class lives at the depth its pigment can light."  ·  Why does Spirogyra float as "pond silk" on the water surface? **Answer.** Because the filament manufactures its own **flotation device**: photosynthesis packs the cells with oxygen and the abundant **mucilage sheath** secreted around the filament traps gas and never wets.…  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Deep dive — pigments classify the algae.** Algal classes are named by colour because colour is the visible summary of the pigment set: chlorophylls plus accessory pigments.
